_comment: x-viral-tracker config. Copy this file to config.json and edit it. Tune everything here; never edit tracker.py to change behavior. All values below are NEUTRAL EXAMPLES — replace queries/niche_terms with your own topic.

apify._comment: Two interchangeable actors return the same tweet schema. Default is kaito: it has no free-tier per-run cap and is the cheapest. apidojo~tweet-scraper is the best-documented alternative but caps output at ~10 items/run on the FREE Apify plan. To switch: set actor to 'apidojo~tweet-scraper' and actor_price_per_tweet_usd to 0.0004. Put your token in the APIFY_TOKEN env var (see .env.example) — do NOT paste it here.

acquire._comment: Cost levers: max_items caps the bill (max_items * actor_price_per_tweet_usd). minimum_favorites is a SERVER-SIDE filter so you never pay for dead posts. freshness_days bounds the time window. queries are X/Twitter search strings — the tool appends 'lang:<language> since:<date> min_faves:<minimum_favorites>' to each. Replace the example queries below with phrases from YOUR niche.
acquire._queries_comment: EXAMPLES ONLY — these are generic 'something new happened' queries. Precision comes from naming specific terms/incumbents in your niche. Widen recall by adding broad catch-all queries; raise precision by naming specific products, people, or keywords. Use standard X search operators (quotes for phrases, OR, parentheses).

relevance_gate._comment: A cheap keyword pre-gate. A post is kept if it satisfies require_any_of. has_github_link=true keeps any post containing a github.com link (useful when tracking open-source tools; set false to disable). niche_terms is a substring OR-list — a post is kept if its text contains any of them. Replace these with YOUR topic keywords.

_suppress_comment: suppress_penalty multiplies the score of a post that uses hype language. Flagged, not deleted, so you still see it (brand_flags in the output). Lower the penalty to be harsher. These terms are topic-neutral quality filters; extend for your niche.

virality._comment: Composite score = weighted sum of each signal normalized to the pull's median (ratio-to-median, capped at normalization_cap), times an age-decay factor. Weights emphasize velocity, spread (reposts/quotes), and bookmarks. reply_like_pivot is the reply/like ratio treated as 'discussion-heavy' (used to normalize the reply_quality term).

baseline._comment: If calibrated:true, these medians normalize scoring across runs (a stable bar). If false, the tracker self-normalizes to the current pull's median (a good cold-start default). Run: python3 tracker.py --calibrate  to populate these from a larger sample of your niche.

output._top_n_comment: 0 = emit EVERY relevance-gated unique drop (virality is only a sort key). Set a positive N to cap how many candidates each run emits.
